data.headword: maʕlele/maʕle rišo mqabəl d- 'sich gegen eine Obrigkeit auflehnen'
data.turoyo: Ǧan: Abuna kəmmi ban 1924 las səryoye madənḥoye, b Botan, b Šərnaq, b Ḥakkari, bəṯər məd maʕlalle rišaye mqabəl di ḥkume, i ḥkume zayiʕo as səryoye maʕərboye ste d lə qaymi li raġlo bam mdiyoṯo xəd Mərde, Diyarbakər, Urfa...
data.translation: Jan: Father, they say that in 1924, concerning the Eastern Syriacs in Botan, Shirnak, Hakkari, after they raised their heads against the government, the government was afraid that the Western Syriacs too would rise to their feet in the cities such as Mardin, Diyarbakir, Urfa...

rationale: Head raising against government is a noun-specific rebellion collocation; mqabəl search has no ʕly parallel. One attestation; retain the complete dependent political context.

summary: II mʕal- and III maʕl- remain separate as in the entry, with its explicit dialect-variation note. The stem assignment follows the supplied surface form, including II mʕalela and III maʕlele; no global normalization is justified.
New III.4 unifies incremental construction of castle, house, walls and kiln. I rise can alternate with III building up in the same procedure, without making I a new building-specific sense.
Voice raising retains existing III.3 and the existing idiom headword. Elliptical lə maʕlət in JTM 3.1/9 is understood from the hush/speech sequence, but a fuller overt-voice context was preferred.
Surrender, nonhostile hand gestures and hand-on-person ʕal constructions must be distinguished. The latter idiom is already recorded; the former are contextual uses of literal raising.

No new ko-Preterit is established from tentative gʕali, and no Turoyo Detransitive box is established by the two Classical Syriac hymn honorifics. teʕliyo is an active Infinitiv despite the inherited box filing.

The parsed III senses contain a nested numbered editorial comment, and Imperativ example 2 conflates two commands. Proposed structural corrections preserve existing substantive sense numbers and all source wording.
Existing III.1/2 embedded in the III.3 editorial comment are not extra senses; the round-1 structural decision remains. New general scalar III.5 follows round-1 III.4.

II mʕaliwaynanne keeps the surface II stem and establishes Infectum-wa; no global II/III merger. maʕlewolən with 1pl L-agent establishes III Preterit-wa. maʕliyowalle remains morphologically ambiguous and is not a second paradigm exemplar.

Ordinary raised heads, a cap and an inviting hand do not create idioms. III.1 Preterit and Infectum already reach five after round 1, so their many proposed thin-cell examples are not added. The road surface could be physical raising or incremental building; do not force that uncertain case into a new sense.

The extended mawʕəlele in the Jonah shade account and mʕalʕalle are not silently regularized. maʕleli at the stuck slipper has an unclear patient and causal sequence. No catch/stir-up senses are inferred from English.
New idioms were searched with əšme li (zero hits) and mqabəl (nine hits, no matching ʕly idiom); original headwords and round-1 proposals checked.
Verify gʕali at 96/224, particularly the vowel and hand/finger agreement, before adding a ko-Preterit box.
Verify Aʕlay at PrS 65/54 as I rise versus III raise; do not assume omitted rider patients from the translation.
Can the recording recover interrupted kmaʕ... at JTM 1.1/27?
Check PrS 40/22–23 translation alignment; the assigned translation does not render the ascent.
Does maʕlela nuro at JTM 5.2/80 specify kindling or intensifying an existing fire? The recorded wording supports only the broader fire-stoking collocation.

Reconcile the inherited war-declaration example 56/33 with ʕln and the unresolved III.2 conditions example 99/13 using their actual passages; neither is supplied here, so neither is reassigned on speculation.
At 78/237, is the implicit object a veil or the brother? Supplied German and inherited English conflict; leave the existing text unchanged pending editorial checking.
Check voice ḥəz spelling at 29/103 and the Classical Syriac honorific derivation at 66/279.
Confirm maʕliyowalle at 1.36/1458 as Preterit-wa versus Infectum-wa; bare maʕliyo in the same verse is also not a secure finite-form exemplar.
Identify mʕalʕalle at 2.29/4667: ʕly expressive form or another root? No second-stem stirring sense proposed.
At 1.46/1994 what does maʕleli index in the slipper incident? At 2.31/5172 how are l Aloho, lu šərurawo and mawʕəlele segmented?
Confirm plural pebble-game Mʕaliwaynanne as II under the inherited dialect variation; and whether 2.35/5537 ʕolən has feathers or birds as subject.
Does educational sohḏuṯo denote a certificate, qualification level or testimony here? Current III.5 classification follows the university context; no degree system is reconstructed.
Restore the umlaut in plural “Bäume”.
rationale: The coordinated subject aw=warde adorns lawns and trees. The supplied translation explicitly has plural bäume; Baume here is a misspelled plural, not the archaic dative singular.

summary: Separate the fused words “blies er”.
rationale: The German verb and following subject pronoun have accidentally been fused.

summary: Correct the dative plural “von den Füssen”.
rationale: Von requires the dative: den Füssen, not der Füsse. The edition has von den Füßen. The proposal retains the entry’s ss spelling convention.

summary: Repair the misplaced word boundary in “Staubwolke herankam”.
rationale: The supplied translation reads eine Staubwolke herankam. The entry has split the same character sequence at the wrong positions, accidentally introducing eher.

summary: Restore the ending in “seine Stimme”.
rationale: Stimme is feminine and is the accusative object of hörte; sein lacks the required -e. The supplied edition repeats the same obvious slip.

summary: Rising water, masonry courses and growing plants extend the subject range of rise; static tall buildings are already represented in 4/81–82.
An inanimate force (waters) can be the l-marked Preterit actor in lifting a swimmer. Literal raising of hands can signal dissent or surrender; this alone does not establish a separate idiom.
Jan house construction confirms round-1 building-up sense; do not re-propose it as literal lifting III.1.
Fire/smoke and growing wheat/herb continue the participant range already noted in round 1; no growth-specific sense.
